When agents use this

After a theme edit, before sharing an interface and during review or CI.

Skills: jig-verify, jig-review.

These are arithmetic checks on declared pairs. They do not prove rendered coverage, colour recognition or visual comfort.

A real finding: Panel and chrome blended together

Before: The coordinator found zero surface steps and reversed light neutrals in the preview.

After / recorded fix: Adjacent layers now require a measured separation; tests deliberately collapse a layer and require rejection.

Why: Passing a text contrast check alone does not make the interface hierarchy visible.

Source: themes/README.md · Pass 7 coordinator findings

From themes/README.md · Pass 7 coordinator findings

Pass 7 coordinator findings

FindingChangeStill needs a visual check
1. Eight types shared four huesEight type angles at 45° intervals, rotated from each source key. Pairwise header checks require 0.045 ΔEOK and 30° hue separation. Type edges/headers stay at least 0.08 ΔEOK and header hues at least 12° from state ink. Working uses its own blue midpoint between type hues.Recognising all eight types on Board, especially Ticket vs Check; judge White board, Dracula and Electric first.
2. Zero surface steps and reversed light neutralsChrome has its own ground. Seven adjacent layer pairs must each differ by at least 0.025 ΔEOK; the real minimum now exceeds 0.03 in every pack. Light neutral steps 1–6 decrease monotonically. Actual card/frame and header/body pairs are checked too.Visible depth without making the light-mode board too grey; inspect frame, card, header, panel and chrome together.
3. Soft-card white bandThe full .map-node background uses the same tint mix as .node-content, so fixed-height cards paint below the content. Selected cards retain their selection ground.The bottom and edges of short-content cards at Middle and Far, including scrolling and selected cards. Static CSS checks cannot prove raster coverage.
4. White board vs Paper unclearThe one-line distinction above explicitly names pure white vs warm paper.Whether both treatments earn their place.
5. Dark cards flat; Electric chrome greyStronger type-tinted headers must differ from the neutral card body by at least 0.10 ΔEOK in dark profiles. Electric chrome is navy; the later Board CSS rule now uses surface-chrome. Components shows eight actual header swatches and adds chrome to its layer ladder.Dark header pop, navy continuity across toolbar/queue/chat, and comfort without glare.
6. Needs you looked olive-brownLight attention fill is orange #ffb989, with separate dark orange ink; the preview uses the checked state/fill pair. Clarity's link was darkened to retain 7:1 on that fill. The checker rejects low-chroma light attention fills.Whether the chip reads clearly as orange/amber and remains the most useful attention signal.

These are implemented changes with static evidence. No browser was launched in this pass.

From themes/README.md · Contrast and measured results

Contrast and measured results

Reading text, links, disabled text, action labels, chip labels, type header labels and chrome text require 4.5:1, or 7:1 in Clarity. Essential control boundaries, type edges, selected boundaries, action fills and focus require 3:1. Primary/secondary/links are checked across ten neutral roles, all five state reading fills and all quiet type surfaces. Every header uses its own type text pair. State text is checked on its matching fill and panel, including the actual attention-chip pair. Chrome labels and chrome boundaries use their dedicated chrome surface; neutral control interiors keep their normal reading roles. Chrome focus rings use the checked chrome boundary against the surrounding chrome; controls inside the light question panel use the ordinary focus role.

Relation lines use canvas. Accent strokes and header hue are redundant decoration. Scrim carries no content. Arbitrary cross-state combinations, text on accent fills, images and opacity are outside this contract. No accessibility or comfort certification follows from these arithmetic checks.

The checker rejects missing, duplicate, unknown or cyclic tokens, malformed manifests/colours, wrong active aliases, unchecked CSS overrides, invalid harmony geometry and report drift. The CSV records every checked pair with its actual hex colours, unrounded decision ratio and threshold. Display minima are floored, never rounded into a pass.
